title: Member Handbook: Counting Acres across a Member's Custom Application and Field Services Plans
content:
Acres are counted across every plan a member holds under Custom Application and Field Services for the crop year, because a field worked once cannot be committed twice. The crop year for this purpose runs 1 September through 31 August, and the acres counted in it are the acres on the member's completed passes across every plan they hold.

### One field, one live plan

The same field may not sit on two live plans for the same crop year, and where a member moves acres between their plans the acres come off one before they go on the other.

### The ceiling on a single plan

A plan may not carry more than its programme's acre ceiling, and acres beyond it go onto a second plan rather than being squeezed in. What is left to work on a plan is the acres enrolled on it less the acres already worked on it.

### The season commitment and the shortfall charge

Season commitment is measured at the end of the crop year on acres actually worked across the plan, and a member who falls short of the acres they committed pays the programme's shortfall charge on the acres not worked, whatever the reason. Acres lost to a weather hold that ran past the end of the season are the one case the charge is waived. Acres reworked under the rework allowance do not count a second time toward the commitment, since they are the same ground.

The programme a plan is written on supplies all three of the figures this section turns on: the acre ceiling the plan may not exceed, the acres the member commits for the crop year, and the charge per committed acre not worked.

### Worked illustration on hypothetical acres

Take a member on a programme whose acre ceiling is 4000 acres and whose commitment is 300 acres, and suppose they enrol 900 acres on one plan. The enrolment is inside the ceiling. Over the season the applicator completes passes totalling 260 acres on that plan, of which 20 acres were a rework of ground already worked once. The commitment is measured on acres actually worked, and the reworked 20 acres are the same ground rather than fresh acres, so the acres that count toward the commitment are 240. The member is 60 acres short of the 300 committed, and the shortfall charge is raised on those 60 acres at the programme's rate per committed acre not worked. Had the shortfall arisen because a weather hold ran past the end of the season, no shortfall charge would be raised at all.
